3107.text: If for a hypothetical reaction, $E_a=0$ at $273 \mathrm{ K}$, then find the ratio of the rate constants at $383 \mathrm{ K}$ and $273 \mathrm{ K}$.
3107.sol:
Relation between activation energy $\left(E_a\right)$ and rate constant (k),
$\Rightarrow \quad k=A e^{-\frac{E_a}{R T}}$
Here, A = frequency factor or pre-exponential
factor.
T = temperature (in K)
R = gas constant
e = mathematical quantity
Now, at $273 \mathrm{~K}, E_a=0 \begin{aligned}$k_1 & =A e^{-$\frac{0}{R \times 273}$} \\
k_1 & =A $\cdot$1 \\
k_1 & =A...(i)
\end{aligned}

Similarly at, 383 K,
$k_2=A e^{-\frac{E_a}{383}}$...(ii)
Ratio of Eqs. (i) and (ii) is

k_2=k_1 e^{-$\frac{E_a}{383}$}

If, $\Delta E_a=0$
k_2=k_1

Hence, ratio of rate constant at $383 \mathrm{~K}$ is 1 .

6459.subject: Mathematics
6459.text: If $\frac{17 x-2}{12 x^2-x-20}=\frac{A}{a x+5}+\frac{B}{3 x+b}$ then $a \cdot A+b \cdot B=$
6459.sol:
Given $\frac{17 x-2}{12 x^2-x-20}=\frac{A}{(a x+5)}+\frac{B}{3 x+b}...(i)$
Now $\frac{17 x-2}{12 x^2-x-20}=\frac{17 x-2}{(3 x-4)(4 x+5)}$
By using partial fraction, RHS can be written as:
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{17 x-2}{12 x^2-x-20}=\frac{P}{(3 x-4)}+\frac{Q}{4 x+5}...(ii) \\
& \Rightarrow 17 x-2=P(4 x+5)+Q(3 x-4)=x(4 P+3 Q)+(5 P-4 Q)
\end{aligned}$
From above equation, we get:
$P=2, \quad Q=3$
Putting above values in equation (ii), we get:
$\frac{17 x-2}{12 x^2-x-20}=\frac{2}{(3 x-4)}+\frac{3}{4 x+5}...(iii)$
Comparing eqn (i) & (iii), we get
$\begin{aligned}
& A=2, B=3, a=-4, b=4 \\
& a \cdot A+b \cdot B=-4.2+(4) \cdot 3=4
\end{aligned}$

\(\begin{aligned} & \quad=x^4\left[-\frac{1}{4 \times 16}+3 \times \frac{1}{8} \times \frac{1}{81}\right]=x^4\left[-\frac{1}{64}+\frac{1}{216}\right] \\ & \therefore \text{ Coefficient of } x^4 \text{ is }\left(-\frac{1}{64}+\frac{1}{216}\right) \\ & \quad=\frac{-216+64}{(64)(216)}=\frac{-152}{(64)(216)}=\frac{-19}{1728}\end{aligned}\)

7485.text: If a complex number $z$ satisfies $\left|z^2-1\right|=|z|^2+1$, then $z$ lies on
7485.sol:
Given, $\quad\left|z^2-1\right|=|z|^2+1$
Let z=x+i y $\begin{aligned}& \Rightarrow \quad\left|( x+i y)^2-1\right|=|x+i y|^2+1 \\
& \Rightarrow\left| x^2-y²+2 i x y-1\right|=\left( x^2+y²\right)+1 \\
& \Rightarrow\left|\left( x^2-y²-1\right)+2 i x y\right|=\left( x^2+y²+1\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \sqrt{\left(x^2-y^2-1\right)^2+4 x^2 y^2}= x^2+y²+1 \\
& \Rightarrow\left( x^2-y²\right)^2+1-2\left( x^2-y²\right)+4 x² y² \\
& =\left( x^2+y²+1\right)^2 \\
& =x⁴+y⁴+2 x² y²+1+2 x²+2 y² \\
& \Rightarrow-2 x² y²-2 x²+4 x² y²=2 x² y²+2 x² \\
& \Rightarrow \quad-2 x²=2 x² \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 4 x²=0 \Rightarrow x=0 \\
& \therefore \quad z=x+i y=0+i y \\
& \Rightarrow \quad z=i y \quad \Rightarrow \quad(x, y)=(0, y) \\
&
\end{aligned} Hence, $ z$ lies on the imaginary axis.$

15684.text: The velocity of an object moving in a straight line path is given as a function of time by \(v=6 t-3 t^2\), where \(v\) is in \(\mathrm{ms}^{-1}, t\) is in \(\mathrm{s}\). The average velocity of the object between, \(t=0\) and \(t=2 \mathrm{~s}\) is
15684.sol:
Given, velocity, \(v=6 t-3 t^2\)
As we know that,
\(v=\frac{d x}{d t}\)
Here, \(x\) is the displacement of the particle.
Now, \(d x=v d t\)
Integrate on the both sides, limit \(t=0\) to \(t=2\), we get
\(\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad x & =\int_0^2 v d t=\int_0^2\left(6 t-3 t^2\right) d t \\ & =\left[\frac{6 t^2}{2}\right]_0^2-\left[\frac{3 t^3}{3}\right]_0^2=\left[3 t^2\right]_0^2-\left[t^3\right]_0^2 \\ & =\left[3(2)^2-3(0)^2\right]-\left[(2)^3-(0)^2\right] \\ & =[12-0]-[8-0]=12-8=4 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}\)
\(\begin{aligned}\text{ Average velocity, } 
v_{\text{avg }} & =\frac{\text{ Total displacement }}{\text{ Total time taken }} \\
& =\frac{4}{2}=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, the average velocity of the object between \(t=0\) to \(t=2 \mathrm{~s}\) is \(2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\).

20654.text: Study the graph between partial pressure and mole fraction of some gases and arrange the gases P, Q, R and S dissolved in $H_2$ O, in the decreasing order of their K_{H} values.
20654.sol:
According to Henry's Law, the partial pressure $p$ of a gas is related to its mole fraction $x$ in the solution by the equation $p = K_H \cdot x$, where $K_H$ is the Henry's Law constant.

The given graph plots partial pressure on the y-axis and mole fraction $x$ on the x-axis. The slope of each line represents the Henry's Law constant $K_H$ for the respective gas.

Comparing the slopes of the lines for gases P, Q, R, and S, we observe that the line for S has the steepest slope, followed by P, then R, and finally Q, which has the smallest slope.

Therefore, the order of the slopes is $S > P > R > Q$.

Since the slope corresponds to the value of $K_H$, the decreasing order of their $K_H$ values is $S > P > R > Q$.

Answer: S > P > R > Q

20677.subject: Chemistry
20677.text: Which of the following does not affect solubility of a gas in liquid?
20677.sol:
The solubility of a gas in a liquid is governed by Henry's Law and the physical properties of the solute and solvent.

The nature of the gas and the liquid determines the intermolecular forces between them, which directly affects solubility.

Pressure affects the solubility of a gas in a liquid according to Henry's Law, where solubility is directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas above the liquid.

Temperature affects the solubility of a gas in a liquid; typically, the solubility of a gas decreases as temperature increases because the dissolution process is generally exothermic.

Concentration is a measure of the amount of solute present in a given quantity of solvent or solution. It is the result of the solubility process, not a factor that determines the solubility itself.

Answer: Concentration

22726.subject: Physics
22726.text: In an inductor of self-inductance $2 \mathrm{ mH}$, current changes with time (in sec) according to the relation, $I=(3 t^2-3 t+8) A$. The emf becomes zero at
22726.sol:
The induced electromotive force (emf) in an inductor is given by the formula $\varepsilon = -L \dfrac{dI}{dt}$.

Given $L = 2 \text{ mH} = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ H}$ and $I = 3t^2 - 3t + 8$.

Differentiating the current $I$ with respect to time $t$:

$\dfrac{dI}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(3t^2 - 3t + 8) = 6t - 3$.

The emf becomes zero when $\dfrac{dI}{dt} = 0$.

Setting the derivative to zero:

$6t - 3 = 0$

$6t = 3$

$t = \dfrac{3}{6} = 0.5 \text{ sec}$.

Answer: 0.5 sec

Initial image distance: $v_1 = f(1+m_1)$
Final image distance: $v_2 = f(1+m_2)$

Given $v_2 - v_1 = x$:

$f(1+m_2) - f(1+m_1) = x$

$f(m_2 - m_1) = x$

$f = \dfrac{x}{m_2 - m_1}$

23432.subject: Physics
23432.text: Applying a constant torque the speed of a flywheel is increased from 1800 rpm to 2400 rpm in 10 seconds. The number of revolutions made by the flywheel during this time is:
23432.sol:
Initial angular velocity $\omega_0 = 1800 \text{ rpm} = \dfrac{1800 \times 2\pi}{60} \text{ rad/s} = 60\pi \text{ rad/s}$.

Final angular velocity $\omega = 2400 \text{ rpm} = \dfrac{2400 \times 2\pi}{60} \text{ rad/s} = 80\pi \text{ rad/s}$.

Time interval $t = 10 \text{ s}$.

Assuming constant angular acceleration $\alpha$, the average angular velocity is $\omega_{avg} = \dfrac{\omega_0 + \omega}{2} = \dfrac{60\pi + 80\pi}{2} = 70\pi \text{ rad/s}$.

Total angular displacement $\theta = \omega_{avg} \times t = 70\pi \times 10 = 700\pi \text{ radians}$.

The number of revolutions $N$ is given by $\theta = N \times 2\pi$.

$N = \dfrac{\theta}{2\pi} = \dfrac{700\pi}{2\pi} = 350$.

Answer: $350$

23875.subject: Biology
23875.text: Which one of the following correctly describes the sequence of events leading to muscle contraction following acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction?
options: Decrease of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ in sarcoplasm, masking of active sites for myosin, 'Z' lines pulled inwards
Increase of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ in sarcoplasm, masking of active sites for myosin, 'Z' lines pulled inwards
Increase of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ in sarcoplasm, unmasking of active sites for myosin, 'Z' lines pulled inwards
Increase of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ in sarcoplasm, unmasking of active sites for myosin, 'Z' lines pulled outwards
23875.sol:
Release of acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction generates an action potential in the sarcolemma.

This action potential spreads through the muscle fibre and causes the release of calcium ions ($\text{Ca}^{++}$) from the sarcoplasmic reticulum into the sarcoplasm.

The increase in $\text{Ca}^{++}$ level leads to the binding of calcium with a subunit of troponin on actin filaments, thereby removing the masking of active sites for myosin.

Utilising the energy from ATP hydrolysis, the myosin head binds to the exposed active sites on actin to form a cross bridge.

This pulls the attached actin filaments towards the centre of the 'A' band. The 'Z' lines attached to these actins are also pulled inwards, thereby causing a shortening of the sarcomere, i.e., contraction.

Answer: Increase of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ in sarcoplasm, unmasking of active sites for myosin, 'Z' lines pulled inwards

25470.text: Let $f: [ 1 . \infty ) \to \mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function such that $f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$ and $3{∫}_{1}^{x}f\left(t\right)dt = xf\left(x\right) - \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}, x \in [ 1, \infty )$. Let $e$ denote the base of the natural logarithm. Then the value of $f\left(e\right)$ is
25470.sol:
Given,

$3{∫}_{1}^{x}f\left(t\right)dt = xf\left(x\right) - \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}$

Now differentiating both side we get,

$⇒ 3f\left(x\right) = f\left(x\right) + x{f}^{'}\left(x\right) - {x}^{2}$

$⇒ x{f}^{'}\left(x\right) - 2f\left(x\right) = {x}^{2}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) - \dfrac{2}{x}f\left(x\right) = x$

Which is a linear differential equation,

$⇒ I . F . = {e}^{- \dfrac{2}{x}dx} = \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}$

Now solution is given by,

$⇒ y\left(\dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right) = ∫ x \times \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}dx = ln ⁡ x + C$

$⇒ y = {x}^{2} ( ln ⁡ x + C )$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = {x}^{2} ( lnx + C )$

Now using given value, $f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$ we get,

$⇒ 0 + C = \dfrac{1}{3} ⇒ C = \dfrac{1}{3}$

So, $f\left(x\right) = {x}^{2}\left(lnx + C\right)$

$⇒ f\left(e\right) = {e}^{2}\left(lne + \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(e\right) = \dfrac{4{e}^{2}}{3}$

25475.text: Let $b$ be a nonzero real number. Suppose $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a differentiable function such that $f\left(0\right) = 1$. If the derivative ${f}^{'}$ of $f$ satisfies the equation ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{{b}^{2} + {x}^{2}}$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R},$ then which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{{b}^{2} + {x}^{2}} ⇒ \dfrac{{f}^{'}\left(x\right)}{f\left(x\right)} = \dfrac{1}{{b}^{2} + {x}^{2}}$

$⇒ lnf\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{b}\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{x}{b} + C$

$∴ f\left(0\right) = 1 ∴ 0 = 0 + C ⇒ C = 0$

$∴ lnf\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{b}\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{x}{b}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = {e}^{\dfrac{1}{b}\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{x}{b}}$

$∴ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = {e}^{\dfrac{1}{b}\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{x}{b}} . \dfrac{1}{{b}^{2} + {x}^{2}} > 0$ for $x \in R$

$⇒ f\left(x\right)$ is increasing for $x \in R$.

$f\left(x\right) . f\left(- x\right) = {e}^{\dfrac{1}{b}\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{x}{b}} \cdot {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{b}\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{x}{b}} = {e}^{0} = 1$.

26797.subject: Physics
26797.text: A tennis ball is dropped on a horizontal smooth surface. It bounces back to its original position after hitting the surface. The force on the ball during the collision is proportional to the length of compression of the ball. Which one of the following sketches describes the variation of its kinetic energy $K$ with $t$time most appropriately? The figures are only illustrative and not to the scale.
26797.sol:
When ball of mass $' m '$ dropped from height and strikes to ground.It's kinetic energy is converting into elastic potential energy due to compression.

So after time $' t '$ its final velocity,

$v = u + at$

$u$ is initial velocity of ball, $a$ is acceleration of ball and $t$ is time.

$⇒ v = 0 + \left(- g\right)t$

$v = - gt$

Negative sign shows downward direction.

Now kinetic energy of ball,

$K . E . = \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\left(- gt\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ K . E . = \dfrac{1}{2}{mg}^{2}{t}^{2}$

$⇒ K . E . ∝ {t}^{2}$

So, it is upward parabola. But after complete compression, $K . E .$ becomes zero, then ball will reshape again. Kinetic energy will not be constant.

33997.text: Let $g\left(x\right)$ be a linear function and $f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}g\left(x\right), & x \le 0 \\ \left(\dfrac{1 + x}{2 + x}\right)\dfrac{1}{x}, & x > 0\end{cases}\right), is continuous at $x = 0$. 33997.sol:
Let, $g\left(x\right) = ax + b$

Now function $f\left(x\right)$ in continuous at $x = 0$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}f\left(x\right) = f\left(0\right)$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{1 + x}{2 + x}\right)\dfrac{1}{x} = b$

$⇒ 0 = b$ 

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = ax$

Now, for $x > 0$

$f\left(x\right) = \left(\dfrac{1 + x}{2 + x}\right)\dfrac{1}{x}$

$⇒ logf\left(x\right) = log\left(\dfrac{1 + x}{2 + x}\right)\dfrac{1}{x}$

$⇒ logf\left(x\right) = \dfrac{log\left(1 + x\right) - log\left(2 + x\right)}{x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{f\left(x\right)} \times {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + x} - \dfrac{1}{2 + x}\right) - \left[log\left(1 + x\right) - log\left(2 + x\right)\right]}{{x}^{2}}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = f\left(x\right)\left\{\dfrac{x\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + x} - \dfrac{1}{2 + x}\right) - \left[log\left(1 + x\right) - log\left(2 + x\right)\right]}{{x}^{2}}\right\}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(1\right) = f\left(1\right)\left\{\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right) - \left[log\left(2\right) - log\left(3\right)\right]}{{1}^{2}}\right\}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(1\right) = \dfrac{2}{3}\left\{\dfrac{1}{6} - log\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)\right\}$

And, $f\left(- 1\right) = g\left(- 1\right) = - a$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{2}{3}log\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) - \dfrac{1}{9}$

Now,  finding $g\left(3\right) = 3a + 0$

$⇒ g\left(3\right) = 2log\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) - \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ g\left(3\right) = log\left(\dfrac{4}{9 ⋅ {e}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}}\right)$

34493.text:
Let the system of linear equations

$x + y + kz = 2$

$2x + 3y - z = 1$

$3x + 4y + 2z = k$

have infinitely many solutions. Then the system

$\left(k + 1\right)x + \left(2k - 1\right)y = 7$

Linear equations $x + y + kz = 2$, $2x + 3y - z = 1 and 3x + 4y + 2z = k$ have infinitely many solutions.

Therefore,

$\left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & k \\ 2 & 3 & - 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 2\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 1\left(10\right) - 1\left(7\right) + k\left(- 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ 10 - 7 - k = 0$

$⇒ 3 - k = 0$

$⇒ k = 3$

For $k = 3$, the second system of equations is

$4x + 5y = 7 \ldots \left(1\right)$

$7x + 8y = 10 \ldots \left(2\right)

Clearly, they have a unique solution

Subtracting \left(1\right)\text{$ and }$\left(2\right), we get

$3x + 3y = 3$

$⇒ x + y = 1$

$

One ball is transferred from Bag $I$ to Bag $II$ and then a ball is draw from Bag $II$. The ball so drawn is found to be black in colour. Then the probability, that the transferred ball is red, is
36628.sol:
Given,

In bag $1 \to 3R, 4B \text{ and } 3W$

And in bag $2 \to 2R, 5B \text{ and } 2W$

Let $A:$ Drawn ball from bag $II$ is black

And let $B:$ Red ball transferred

Now by total probability theorem we have $P\left(A\right) = \dfrac{3}{9} \times \dfrac{5}{10} + \dfrac{4}{9} \times \dfrac{6}{10} + \dfrac{3}{9} \times \dfrac{5}{10} = \dfrac{54}{90}$

And $P\left(A ∩ B\right) = \dfrac{3}{9} \times \dfrac{5}{10}$

So, by bayes theorem we have, $P\left(\dfrac{B}{A}\right) = \dfrac{P\left(A ∩ B\right)}{P\left(A\right)}$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{3}{9} \times \dfrac{5}{10}}{\dfrac{3}{9} \times \dfrac{5}{10} + \dfrac{4}{9} \times \dfrac{6}{10} + \dfrac{3}{9} \times \dfrac{5}{10}}$

$= \dfrac{15}{15 + 24 + 15} = \dfrac{15}{54} = \dfrac{5}{18}$

40867.subject: Physics
40867.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: If$E$be the total energy of a satellite moving around the earth, then its potential energy will be $\dfrac{E}{2}$.

Statement II: The kinetic energy of a satellite revolving in an orbit is equal to the half the magnitude of total energy $E$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
40867.sol:
Let $m$ be the mass of the satellite.

The potential energy of the satellite is

$U = \dfrac{- GMm}{r}$

The velocity of the satellite is given by

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{r}}$

Kinetic energy is given by

$K = \dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{2} = \dfrac{m}{2}\dfrac{GM}{r} = \dfrac{GMm}{2r}$

The total mechanical energy is the sum of potential and kinetic energy. So,

$T = K + U = \dfrac{GMm}{2r} - \dfrac{GMm}{r} = - \dfrac{GMm}{2r}$

Hence, both the statements are false.

41194.subject: Physics
41194.text: Two blocks ($P$ and $Q$) with respectively masses $2$ kg and $1.5$ kg are joined by a massless thread. These blocks are mounted on a frictionless pulley which is fixed on the edge of a cube ($S$), as shown in the figure below. Block $P$ is positioned on the top surface which has no friction and block $Q$ is in contact with side-surface, having coefficient friction $\mu$. The cube ($S$) moves towards the right with acceleration of $\dfrac{g}{2}$, where $g$ is gravitational acceleration. During this movement the block $P$ and $Q$ remain stationary. The value of $\mu$ is _______. (take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
41194.sol:
Let us analyze the forces acting on blocks $P$ and $Q$ in the non-inertial frame of reference of the cube $S$, which is moving to the right with an acceleration $a = \dfrac{g}{2} = 5 \text{ m/s}^2$.

In this frame, a pseudo force acts on both blocks towards the left.

For block $P$ (mass $m_P = 2 \text{ kg}$):
The forces in the horizontal direction are the tension $T$ in the string (acting towards the right) and the pseudo force $F_{pP}$ (acting towards the left). Since block $P$ is stationary relative to the cube and there is no friction on the top surface:
$T = m_P a = 2 \times 5 = 10 \text{ N}$

For block $Q$ (mass $m_Q = 1.5 \text{ kg}$):
The horizontal forces are the normal reaction $N$ from the side surface of the cube (acting towards the right) and the pseudo force $F_{pQ}$ (acting towards the left). Since block $Q$ is stationary horizontally relative to the cube:
$N = m_Q a = 1.5 \times 5 = 7.5 \text{ N}$

The vertical forces acting on block $Q$ are the downward gravitational force $m_Q g$, the upward tension $T$, and the frictional force $f$.
The downward force is $m_Q g = 1.5 \times 10 = 15 \text{ N}$.
Since $m_Q g > T$ ($15 \text{ N} > 10 \text{ N}$), the block has a tendency to slide downwards, so the static friction $f$ must act upwards.
For vertical equilibrium of block $Q$:
$T + f = m_Q g$
$10 + f = 15 \Rightarrow f = 5 \text{ N}$

To keep the block stationary, the required friction must be less than or equal to the maximum static friction ($f \le \mu N$). Assuming the limiting case to find the value of $\mu$:
$\mu N = f$
$\mu (7.5) = 5$
$\mu = \dfrac{5}{7.5} = \dfrac{2}{3} \approx 0.67$

Answer: $0.67$

42658.subject: Physics
42658.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
A. $\sin^2 \omega t$I. Periodic with time period $T = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$ but not simple harmonic motion (SHM)
B. $\sin^3(2\omega t)$II. Periodic with time period $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$ but Not SHM
C. $\sin(\omega t) + \cos(\pi \omega t)$III. Periodic with time period $T = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$ and SHM
D. $\cos\omega t + \cos 2\omega t$IV. Non-periodic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
42658.sol:
For A: $y = \sin^2 \omega t = \dfrac{1 - \cos 2\omega t}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \cos 2\omega t$

This represents simple harmonic motion (SHM) about the mean position $y = \dfrac{1}{2}$ with an angular frequency of $2\omega$. The time period is $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{2\omega} = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$. Thus, A matches III.

For B: $y = \sin^3(2\omega t) = \dfrac{3\sin 2\omega t - \sin 6\omega t}{4}$

This is a superposition of two SHMs with angular frequencies $2\omega$ and $6\omega$. It is periodic but not SHM. The time period is the LCM of $T_1 = \dfrac{2\pi}{2\omega} = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$ and $T_2 = \dfrac{2\pi}{6\omega} = \dfrac{\pi}{3\omega}$, which is $T = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$. Thus, B matches I.

For C: $y = \sin(\omega t) + \cos(\pi \omega t)$

The angular frequencies are $\omega_1 = \omega$ and $\omega_2 = \pi \omega$. The ratio $\dfrac{\omega_1}{\omega_2} = \dfrac{1}{\pi}$ is an irrational number. Therefore, the function is non-periodic. Thus, C matches IV.

For D: $y = \cos \omega t + \cos 2\omega t$

This is a superposition of two SHMs with angular frequencies $\omega$ and $2\omega$. It is periodic but not SHM. The time period is the LCM of $T_1 = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$ and $T_2 = \dfrac{2\pi}{2\omega} = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega}$, which is $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$. Thus, D matches II.

The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

45903.text: The molal freezing point depression constant for benzene $\left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_6\right)$ is $4.90 \mathrm{~K} \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. Selenium exists as a polymer of the type $\mathrm{Se}_x$. When 3.26 g of selenium is dissolved in 226 g of benzene, the observed freezing point is $0.112^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ lower than that of pure benzene. The molecular formula of selenium is (atomic mass of $\mathrm{Se}=78.8 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$)
45903.sol:
To calculate the molar mass of selenium (Se)
$M_B=\frac{K_f \times W_B}{\Delta T_f \times W_A}$
Mas of selenium $\left(W_B\right)=3.26 \mathrm{~g}$
Mass of benzene $\left(W_A\right)=226 \mathrm{~g}=0.226 \mathrm{~kg}$
Depression in freezing point $\left(\Delta T_f\right)=0.112^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$
Molar depression constant $\left(K_f\right)=4.9 \mathrm{~K} \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \therefore M_B=\frac{\left(4.9 \mathrm{~K} \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right)(3.26 \mathrm{~g})}{(0.112 \mathrm{~K})(0.226 \mathrm{~kg})}=631.08 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
Given, gram atomic mass of selenium
$=78.8 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$
For $\mathrm{Se}_x\left(78.8 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right)=631.08 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
or, $\quad x=\frac{631.08 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}}{78.8 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}}=8$
Thus, molecular formula of selenium $=\mathrm{Se}_8$

46433.text: Velocity is given by $v=4 t(1-2 t)$, then find time at which velocity is maximum
46433.sol:
To find value of time at which velocity is maximum, taking differentiation of v with respect to time
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}=0$
Here, $v=4 t(l-2 t)$
$\begin{array}{lc} & \mathrm{v}=4 \mathrm{t}-8 \mathrm{t}^2 \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dt}}\left(4 \mathrm{t}-8 \mathrm{t}^2\right)=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 4-16 \mathrm{t}=0 \\ \Rightarrow & \mathrm{t}=\frac{1}{4} \mathrm{~s}=0.25 \mathrm{~s}\end{array}$
Again taking differentiation,
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{d}^2 v}{\mathrm{dt}^2}=-16 \lt 0$
So, at $\mathrm{t}=0.25 \mathrm{~s}$ velocity is maximum.

48573.text: The maximum value of $\frac{\log x}{x}$ in $(2, \infty)$ is
48573.sol:
$\text{ Let }$ y=$\frac{\log x}{x}$ On differentiating w.r.t. x, we get $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{x \cdot \frac{1}{x}-\log x \cdot 1}{x^{2}}=\frac{1-\log x}{x^{2}}$ For maxima, put $\frac{d y}{d x}=0\begin{array}{lc}\Rightarrow & \frac{1-\log x}{x^{2}}=0 \\ \Rightarrow & \log x=1 \\ \Rightarrow & x=e\end{array}$
Now, $\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=\frac{x^{2}\left(-\frac{1}{x}\right)-(1-\log x) 2 x}{\left(x^{2}\right)^{2}}$
At $\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{e}, \frac{\mathrmd^{2} \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{dx^{2 }} \leq 0, \text{ maxima }}\therefore$ The maximum value at $\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{e}$ is $\mathrm{y}=\frac{\log \mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{e}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}$

48632.sol:
The given expression is $\dfrac{x^3 + 3x^2 + 3x + 1}{x^4 + 4x^3 + 6x^2 + 4x + 1}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{3}$

54221.text: Two bodies of different masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ have equal momenta. Their kinetic energies $E_1$ and $E_2$ are in the ratio
54221.sol:
Given - Momentum of two bodies are same i.e. $p_1=p_2$ and mass of two bodies $m_1 and m_2$
The relationship between the kinetic energy (KE) and Linear momentum ( p ) is -
Momentum of first body whose mass is $\mathrm{m}_1$.
$p=\sqrt{2 m_1 K E_1}\qquad ...\mathrm{(1)}$
Momentum of second body whose mass is $\mathrm{m}_2p=\sqrt{2 m_2 K E_2}\qquad ...\mathrm{(2)}$
Divide equation (1) and (2).
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{p}{p}=\frac{\sqrt{2 m_1 K E_1}}{\sqrt{2 m_2 K E_2}} \\
& \sqrt{2 m_2 K E_2}=\sqrt{2 m_1 K E_1}
\end{aligned}$
By squaring both side, we get

\end{aligned}$

54887.subject: Chemistry
54887.text: Which of the following compounds has lowest solubility in water?
54887.sol:
The solubility of organic compounds in water depends on their ability to form hydrogen bonds with water molecules. Polar groups like $\mathrm{-OH}$ and $\mathrm{-NO_2}$ tend to enhance solubility through hydrogen bonding interactions.

Phenol (A) contains a hydroxyl group capable of forming hydrogen bonds with water, resulting in moderate solubility.

p-Cresol (B) also contains a hydroxyl group but includes a hydrophobic methyl group that increases the non-polar character of the molecule, reducing its hydrogen bonding capacity and solubility compared to phenol.

o-Nitrophenol (C) features both hydroxyl and nitro groups in ortho position. The proximity enables intramolecular hydrogen bonding between these groups, which significantly reduces the availability of the hydroxyl group for intermolecular hydrogen bonding with water. Consequently, o-nitrophenol exhibits the lowest solubility among these compounds.

p-Nitrophenol (D) contains hydroxyl and nitro groups in para position, preventing intramolecular hydrogen bonding. Both groups remain available for strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding with water, resulting in the highest solubility.

The solubility order is p-nitrophenol > phenol > p-cresol > o-nitrophenol.

55437.text: Which from following oils is mainly a saturated fats?
55437.sol:
Saturated fats are typically solid at room temperature and contain single bonds between carbon atoms in their fatty acid chains.

Coconut oil is composed of approximately $80\%$ to $90\%$ saturated fat, primarily lauric acid, myristic acid, and palmitic acid.

Olive oil is mainly composed of monounsaturated fats (oleic acid).

Safflower oil and fish oil are rich in polyunsaturated fats (such as linoleic acid and omega-3 fatty acids, respectively).

Therefore, coconut oil is mainly a saturated fat.

Answer: Coconut oil

55657.text:
Identify final products in the following sequence of reactions
$\text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{H}^+}} \text{intermediate} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{Ni}, \Delta}}^{\large{\text{H}_2}} \text{Products}$
55657.sol:
The first step is the Fischer esterification reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst. The reaction produces an ester as the intermediate.

$\text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{RCOOR'} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

The intermediate formed is the ester $\text{RCOOR'}$.

The second step involves the catalytic hydrogenation (hydrogenolysis) of the ester using hydrogen gas over a nickel catalyst at high temperature. This process cleaves the ester bond, reducing the acyl group ($\text{RCO}-$) to a primary alcohol and releasing the alkoxy group ($-\text{OR'}$) as another alcohol.

$\text{RCOOR'} + 2\text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni}, \Delta} \text{RCH}_2\text{OH} + \text{R'OH}$

Thus, the final products are $\text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$ and $\text{R'OH}$.

Answer: $\text{RCH}_2\text{OH} + \text{R'}-\text{OH}$

56048.subject: Chemistry
56048.text:
For a reaction,
$A \rightarrow B$, rate equation is '$r=K[A]^{{}^{\circ}}$'
If initial concentration of reactant is 'a' $\mathrm{mol } \mathrm{dm}^{-3}$ find half life time of reaction.
56048.sol:
The reaction $A \rightarrow B$ follows a zero-order rate law $r = K[A]^0$, where the rate is independent of reactant concentration.

The integrated rate law for zero-order kinetics is $[A]_t = [A]_0 - Kt$.

At half-life $t_{1/2}$, the concentration reduces to $[A]_{t_{1/2}} = \frac{[A]_0}{2}$. Substituting into the rate law:

$\frac{[A]_0}{2} = [A]_0 - K t_{1/2}$

Solving for $t_{1/2}$ yields:

$K t_{1/2} = [A]_0 - \frac{[A]_0}{2} = \frac{[A]_0}{2}$

$t_{1/2} = \frac{[A]_0}{2K}$

Given $[A]_0 = a$, the half-life becomes $t_{1/2} = \frac{a}{2K}$, which corresponds to option D.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

58398.text: Which of the following is not a basis of classification of polymers ?
58398.sol:
Polymers are broadly classified on the basis of the following parameters:

1. Source (Natural, semi-synthetic, and synthetic polymers)
2. Structure (Linear, branched-chain, and cross-linked polymers)
3. Mode of polymerisation or method of preparation (Addition and condensation polymers)
4. Molecular forces (Elastomers, fibres, thermoplastics, and thermosetting polymers)

Polymers are not classified on the basis of the number of monomers. (Note: Based on the types of monomers, they are classified into homopolymers and copolymers, but not on the number of monomers).

Answer: Number of monomers

58618.text: What is oxidation state of oxygen in $\text{OF}_2$ and in $\text{KO}_2$ respectively?
58618.sol:
In $\text{OF}_2$, fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen and always has an oxidation state of $-1$.

Let the oxidation state of oxygen in $\text{OF}_2$ be $x$.

$x + 2(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +2$

In $\text{KO}_2$, potassium is an alkali metal and always has an oxidation state of $+1$.

Let the oxidation state of oxygen in $\text{KO}_2$ be $y$.

$+1 + 2y = 0 \Rightarrow y = -1/2$

The oxidation states of oxygen in $\text{OF}_2$ and $\text{KO}_2$ are $+2$ and $-1/2$ respectively.

Answer: $+2$ and $-1/2$

60401.text: A kite is $120 \mathrm{ m}$ high and $130 \mathrm{ m}$ of string is out. If the kite is moving away horizontally at the rate of $39 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm\sec$, then the rate at which the string is being out, is

Let 'P' be the position of the kite and PR be the string.
Let $\mathrm{QR}=x$ and $\mathrm{PR}=y$
By Pythagoras theorem,
$\begin{aligned}
& -\mathrm{PR}^2=\mathrm{PQ}^2+\mathrm{QR}^2 \\
& \Rightarrow y^2=(120)^2+x^2... (i)
\end{aligned}$
Differentiating w.r.t.t, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& 2 y \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 x \frac{\mathrm{d} x}{\mathrm{dt}} \\
& \Rightarrow y \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{dt}}=x \frac{\mathrm{d} x}{\mathrm{dt}}... (ii)
\end{aligned}$
Now, kite is moving away horizontally at the rate of $39 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm\sec$.
$\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad & \frac{\mathrm{d} x}{\mathrm{dt}}=39 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm\sec \\
& \text{$ From $(i), } \\
& (130)^2=(120)^2+x^2 \\
\Rightarrow & x^2=16900-14400 \\
\Rightarrow & x^2=2500 \\
\Rightarrow & x=50 \\
& \text{ From (ii), } \\
& 130 \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{dt}}=50 \times 39 \\
\therefore \quad & \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{50 \times 39}{130}=15 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm\sec
\end{aligned}$

60561.subject: Mathematics
60561.text: If the area bounded by $y = x^3 + ax$ (where $a > 0$), the $x$-axis and the lines $x = -2$ and $x = 1$ is $\dfrac{37}{4}$ square units, then $\ldots$
60561.sol:
Given the curve $y = x^3 + ax$ with $a > 0$, the roots of $y = 0$ are given by $x(x^2 + a) = 0$. Since $a > 0$, the only real root is $x = 0$.

For $x \in [-2, 0]$, $y \le 0$, and for $x \in [0, 1]$, $y \ge 0$.

The required area $A$ is given by:

$A = \int_{-2}^{0} -(x^3 + ax) dx + \int_{0}^{1} (x^3 + ax) dx$

$A = -\left[ \dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{ax^2}{2} \right]_{-2}^{0} + \left[ \dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{ax^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{1}$

$A = -\left( 0 - \left( \dfrac{16}{4} + \dfrac{4a}{2} \right) \right) + \left( \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{a}{2} -0\right)$

$A = (4 + 2a) + \left( \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{a}{2} \right)$

$A = \dfrac{17}{4} + \dfrac{5a}{2}$

Given that the area is $\dfrac{37}{4}$ square units:

$\dfrac{17}{4} + \dfrac{5a}{2} = \dfrac{37}{4}$

$\dfrac{5a}{2} = \dfrac{20}{4}$

$\dfrac{5a}{2} = 5 \Rightarrow a = 2$

Answer: $a = 2$

62015.subject: Mathematics
62015.text: Let $\mathrm{f}: \mathbb{R}-\{2\} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}-\{1\}$ defined by $\mathrm{f}(x)=\frac{x-3}{x-2}$ and $\mathrm{g}: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ defined by $\mathrm{g}(x)=3 \mathrm{x}-2$, then sum of all values of $x$ for which $\mathrmf^{-1}(x)+\mathrmg^{-1}(x)=\frac{19}{6}$ is
62015.sol:
Given functions are $f(x) = \frac{x - 3}{x - 2}$ and $g(x) = 3x - 2$.

The inverse function $f^{-1}(x)$ is determined by setting $y = f(x)$ and solving for $x$ after interchanging variables:

$x = \frac{y - 3}{y - 2} \implies x(y - 2) = y - 3 \implies xy - y = 2x - 3 \implies y(x - 1) = 2x - 3 \implies f^{-1}(x) = \frac{2x - 3}{x - 1}$, with domain $\mathbb{R} - \{1\}$.

Similarly, $g^{-1}(x)$ yields $x = 3y - 2 \implies y = \frac{x + 2}{3}$, so $g^{-1}(x) = \frac{x + 2}{3}$, with domain $\mathbb{R}$.

Set $f^{-1}(x) + g^{-1}(x) = \frac{19}{6}$:

$\frac{2x - 3}{x - 1} + \frac{x + 2}{3} = \frac{19}{6}$.

Combining terms with common denominator $3(x - 1)$:

$\frac{3(2x - 3) + (x - 1)(x + 2)}{3(x - 1)} = \frac{19}{6}$.

Expanding numerator: $6x - 9 + x^2 + 2x - x - 2 = x^2 + 7x - 11$.

$\frac{x^2 + 7x - 11}{3(x - 1)} = \frac{19}{6}$.

Cross-multiplying: $6(x^2 + 7x - 11) = 57(x - 1)$.

62190.text:
$\displaystyle\int e^{2x} \dfrac{2(\sin 2x \cos 2x - 1)}{2 \sin^2 2x} \, dx = A \, e^{2x} \cot 2x + c$
(Where c is the constant of integration.), then $A^3 =$
62190.sol:
Let the given integral be $I$.

$I = \int e^{2x} \dfrac{2(\sin 2x \cos 2x - 1)}{2 \sin^2 2x} \, dx$

$I = \int e^{2x} \left( \dfrac{\sin 2x \cos 2x}{\sin^2 2x} - \dfrac{1}{\sin^2 2x} \right) \, dx$

$I = \int e^{2x} (\cot 2x - \csc^2 2x) \, dx$

We know the standard integral form: $\int e^{ax} (a f(x) + f'(x)) \, dx = e^{ax} f(x) + c$.

Let $a = 2$ and $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{2} \cot 2x$.

Then $a f(x) = 2 \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \cot 2x \right) = \cot 2x$.

Differentiating $f(x)$ with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{2} (-\csc^2 2x) \times 2 = -\csc^2 2x$

Substituting these into the integral, we get:

$I = \int e^{2x} (2 f(x) + f'(x)) \, dx = e^{2x} f(x) + c$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} e^{2x} \cot 2x + c$

Comparing this with the given expression $A \, e^{2x} \cot 2x + c$, we find:

$A = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Therefore, $A^3 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \dfrac{1}{8}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{8}$

62731.text: If $\quad \mathbf{f}(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cl}\frac{1-\cos 4 x}{x^2} & \text{ if } x < 0 \\ \frac{a}{\sqrt{x}} & \text{ if } x=0 \\ \frac{(16+\sqrt{x})^{\frac{1}{2}}-4}{(16+\sqrt{x})} & \text{ if } x > 0\end{array}\right.$ is continuous at $x=0$ Then $a=$
62731.sol:
To ensure continuity at $x=0$, the left-hand limit, right-hand limit, and function value must satisfy:

$\lim_{x \to 0^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 0^+} f(x) = f(0)$

From the definition, $f(0) = a$.

The left-hand limit uses the standard form $\frac{1 - \cos kx}{x^2}$ with $k=4$, yielding:

$\lim_{x \to 0^-} \frac{1 - \cos 4x}{x^2} = \frac{4^2}{2} = 8$

The right-hand limit evaluates directly:

$\lim_{x \to 0^+} \frac{\sqrt{16 + \sqrt{x}} - 4}{16 + \sqrt{x}} = \frac{0}{16} = 0$

Since $8 \neq 0$, no value of $a$ produces continuity with the given definition. However, the left-hand limit calculation and available options suggest $a=8$ is the intended answer, assuming the right-hand expression contains a typo.

The value ensuring continuity is therefore:

$\boxed{8}$

63159.subject: Mathematics
63159.text: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} \cos\alpha & -\sin\alpha & 0 \\ \sin\alpha & \cos\alpha & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$. If $B = \text{adj}\,A$, then the matrix $B^{-1}$ is equal to...
63159.sol:
The determinant of matrix $A$ is given by

$|A| = \cos\alpha(\cos\alpha - 0) - (-\sin\alpha)(\sin\alpha - 0) + 0$

$|A| = \cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha = 1$

We know the property of adjoint of a matrix:

$A(\text{adj}\,A) = |A|I$

Substituting $|A| = 1$, we get

$A(\text{adj}\,A) = I$

$\Rightarrow \text{adj}\,A = A^{-1}$

It is given that $B = \text{adj}\,A$, so

$B = A^{-1}$

Taking the inverse on both sides, we obtain

$B^{-1} = (A^{-1})^{-1} = A$

Answer: $A$

66552.subject: Physics
66552.text: Which one of the four graphs showing lines P, Q, R and S between maximum kinetic energy (E) and intensity of incident radiation (I) is correct?
66552.sol:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is given by:

$E = h\nu - \Phi$

where $h$ is Planck's constant, $\nu$ is the frequency of incident radiation, and $\Phi$ is the work function of the material.

From this equation, it is clear that the maximum kinetic energy (E$) depends only on the frequency of the incident radiation and the nature of the material. It is completely independent of the intensity (I$) of the incident radiation, provided the frequency is above the threshold frequency.

Therefore, the graph between maximum kinetic energy (E$) and intensity (I$) will be a straight horizontal line parallel to the intensity axis. Line P correctly represents this behavior.

Answer: P

66799.text: A coil of $n$ turns and resistance $R \Omega$ is connected in series with resistance $\mathrm{R} / 4$. The combination is moved for time t second through magnetic flux $\phi_1$ to $\phi_2$. The induced current in the circuit is
66799.sol:
The total circuit resistance combines the coil resistance $R$ with the series resistor of $R/4$:

$R_{\text{total}} = R + \frac{R}{4} = \frac{5R}{4}$

By Faraday's law, the magnitude of induced EMF is $E = n \frac{\Delta \phi}{t} = n \frac{(\phi_1 - \phi_2)}{t}$, as the flux decreases from $\phi_1$ to $\phi_2$.

Applying Ohm’s law yields the current:

$I = \frac{E}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{n (\phi_1 - \phi_2)}{t} \cdot \frac{4}{5R} = \frac{4n (\phi_1 - \phi_2)}{5Rt}$

The resulting expression corresponds to option B.

The upward force due to surface tension is $F_T = T \times L$, where $T$ is the surface tension and $L$ is the inner circumference of the capillary tube. Given that $F_T = 98$ dyne and the surface tension of water is $7 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{N\,m}^{-1}$, convert $T$ to CGS units to maintain consistency with the force unit.

Since $1\,\mathrm{N} = 10^5$ dyne and $1\,\mathrm{m} = 100\,\mathrm{cm}$:

$T = 7 \times 10^{-2} \frac{\mathrm{N}}{\mathrm{m}} = 7 \times 10^{-2} \times \frac{10^5\,\mathrm{dyne}}{100\,\mathrm{cm}} = 70\,\frac{\mathrm{dyne}}{\mathrm{cm}}$.

Substituting into $F_T = T L$ gives:

$98 = 70 L$.

Solving for $L$ yields $L = 98 / 70 = 1.4\,\mathrm{cm}$, the inner circumference. Therefore, the correct answer is A.

68669.subject: Physics
68669.text: A mass $m_1$ performs S.H.M. with amplitude A which is connected to horizontal spring. While mass $m_1$ passing through mean position, another mass $m_2$ (m_2 < m_1$) is placed on it so that both masses move together with amplitude $A_1$. The ratio of $A/A_1$ is$
68669.sol:
Velocity of mass $m_1$ at the mean position is given by $v = A\omega = A\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m_1}}$.

When mass $m_2$ is placed on $m_1$, the horizontal momentum of the system is conserved.

$m_1 v = (m_1 + m_2)v_1$

$v_1 = \dfrac{m_1 v}{m_1 + m_2}$

The new angular frequency of the system is $\omega_1 = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m_1 + m_2}}$.

The new amplitude $A_1$ is related to the new maximum velocity $v_1$ by $v_1 = A_1 \omega_1$.

Substituting the values of $v_1 and \omega_1$:

$A_1 \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m_1 + m_2}} = \dfrac{m_1}{m_1 + m_2} A \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m_1}}$

$A_1 = A \dfrac{m_1}{m_1 + m_2} \sqrt{\dfrac{m_1 + m_2}{m_1}}$

$A_1 = A \sqrt{\dfrac{m_1}{m_1 + m_2}}$

Rearranging to find the ratio $\dfrac{A}{A_1}$:

$\dfrac{A}{A_1} = \left[\dfrac{m_1 + m_2}{m_1}\right]^{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

Answer: $\left[\dfrac{m_1 + m_2}{m_1}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}$

69201.subject: Physics
69201.text: Moment of inertia of a thin uniform rod rotating about the perpendicular axis passing through its centre is 'I'. If the same rod is bent in the form of ring, its moment of inertia about the diameter is ' $\mathrm{I}_1{ }^{\prime}$. If $I_1=x I$, then the value of ' $x$ ' is
69201.sol:
The moment of inertia of a thin uniform rod about its center is $I = \frac{1}{12}ML^2$.

When bent into a ring of radius $R$, the circumference equals the rod length: $L = 2\pi R$, so $R = \frac{L}{2\pi}$. The moment of inertia about a diameter becomes $I_1 = \frac{1}{2}MR^2 = \frac{1}{2}M\left(\frac{L}{2\pi}\right)^2 = \frac{ML^2}{8\pi^2}$.

With $I_1 = xI$, we substitute: $\frac{ML^2}{8\pi^2} = x\left(\frac{1}{12}ML^2\right)$. Canceling $ML^2$ yields $\frac{1}{8\pi^2} = \frac{x}{12}$, so $x = \frac{12}{8\pi^2} = \frac{3}{2\pi^2}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

70500.text: An organ pipe has fundamental frequency 80 Hz. If its one end is closed, the frequencies produced will be (in Hz ) (Neglect end correction)
70500.sol:
An organ pipe of length $L$ with fundamental frequency $80\text{ Hz}$ is initially open, satisfying $\frac{v}{2L} = 80$, where $v$ is the speed of sound.

When one end is closed, it becomes a closed pipe with fundamental frequency $f_{closed} = \frac{v}{4L} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 80 = 40\text{ Hz}$.

Closed pipes produce only odd harmonics: $f_{closed}, 3f_{closed}, 5f_{closed}, 7f_{closed}, \ldots$

Substituting $40\text{ Hz}$ yields the sequence $40, 120, 200, 280, \ldots\text{ Hz}$, which corresponds to option C.

70949.subject: Biology
70949.text: Glucose is phosphorylated to Glucose-6-Phosphate by the enzyme Glucokinase using a molecule of ATP. To which category of enzymes does the Glucokinase belong?
70949.sol:
Glucokinase catalyzes the transfer of a phosphate group from ATP to glucose, forming glucose-6-phosphate and ADP.

Enzymes that catalyze the transfer of a functional group (such as a phosphate, methyl, or amino group) from one molecule to another are classified as transferases.

Since glucokinase transfers a phosphate group, it belongs to the transferase category of enzymes.

Answer: Transferase.

71467.subject: Biology
71467.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): In aerobic respiration, hydrogen removed from respiratory material combines with oxygen to form water.
Statement (II): Removal of hydrogen from respiratory materials is the primary process in respiration.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
71467.sol:
Statement (I) is correct because in aerobic respiration, the final electron (and proton) acceptor is molecular oxygen. The hydrogen atoms removed from respiratory substrates during glycolysis and the Krebs cycle are transferred to coenzymes (NAD^+ and FAD), which then pass them to the electron transport chain. Ultimately, oxygen accepts these electrons and protons to form water.

Statement (II) is correct because respiration is essentially an oxidative process. The primary chemical event in the oxidation of respiratory substrates (like glucose) is dehydrogenation, which is the stepwise removal of hydrogen atoms from the substrate to release energy.

Therefore, both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.

Answer: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.

71581.subject: Biology
71581.text:
Given below are two statements related to the apoplast pathway:
Statement (I): When some amount of water passes across the root through the cell wall and the intercellular spaces of cortical cells of root, it is called apoplast pathway.
Statement (II): An additional apoplastic route that allows direct access to the xylem and phloem is along the margins of secondary roots.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
71581.sol:
Statement (I) is correct: The apoplast pathway involves the movement of water exclusively through the non-living parts of the plant, which include the intercellular spaces and the cell walls. In the root cortex, water moves freely through this pathway because the cortical cells are loosely packed and offer no resistance to water movement.

Statement (II) is correct: The inner boundary of the cortex, the endodermis, usually blocks the apoplastic movement of water into the vascular cylinder due to the presence of the water-impermeable Casparian strip. However, secondary (lateral) roots originate endogenously from the pericycle and grow outward, breaking through the endodermis and cortex. This disruption creates a gap in the Casparian strip along the margins of the emerging secondary roots, providing an additional apoplastic bypass that allows water and solutes direct access to the vascular tissues (xylem and phloem).

Therefore, both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.

Answer: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.

71881.sol:
Strong electrolytes are substances that completely dissociate into ions in aqueous solutions. They generally include strong acids, strong bases, and soluble salts.

$\text{CaCl}_2$ is a soluble salt that dissociates completely into $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ and $\text{Cl}^{-}$ ions in aqueous solution, making it a strong electrolyte.

$\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is a strong base but is only sparingly soluble in water.

$\text{NH}_3$ is a weak base and $\text{HCN}$ is a weak acid, meaning they only partially dissociate in water and are therefore weak electrolytes.

Answer: $\text{CaCl}_2$

72101.text: The angular momentum of an electron in Bohr's hydrogen atom having energy $-0.544$ eV is (h = Planck's constant)
72101.sol:
The energy of an electron in the $n$-th orbit of a hydrogen atom is given by $E_n = -\dfrac{13.6}{n^2}$ eV.

Given $E_n = -0.544$ eV.

$-\dfrac{13.6}{n^2} = -0.544$

$n^2 = \dfrac{13.6}{0.544} = 25$

$n = 5$

The angular momentum of an electron in the $n$-th orbit is $L = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$.

Substituting $n = 5$, we get $L = \dfrac{5h}{2\pi}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{5h}{2\pi}$

72301.subject: Physics
72301.text: A train accelerates from rest at a constant rate 'p' for some time (attains velocity 'v') and then retards to rest at the constant rate 'q'. If the total distance covered by the train is 's', then the velocity 'v' of the train is
72301.sol:
Let $s_1$ be the distance covered during acceleration and $s_2$ be the distance covered during retardation.

Using the third equation of motion for the acceleration phase:
$v^2 = u^2 + 2as_1$
$v^2 = 0 + 2ps_1 \Rightarrow s_1 = \dfrac{v^2}{2p}$

For the retardation phase:
$0 = v^2 - 2qs_2 \Rightarrow s_2 = \dfrac{v^2}{2q}$

Total distance $s = s_1 + s_2$
$s = \dfrac{v^2}{2p} + \dfrac{v^2}{2q}$
$s = \dfrac{v^2}{2} \left( \dfrac{1}{p} + \dfrac{1}{q} \right)$
$s = \dfrac{v^2}{2} \left( \dfrac{p+q}{pq} \right)$

Solving for $v$:
$v^2 = \dfrac{2pq}{p+q} s$
$v = \left( \left( \dfrac{2pq}{p+q} \right) \times s \right)^{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

Answer: $\left( \left( \dfrac{2pq}{p+q} \right) \times s \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}$

75149.subject: General Ability
75149.text:
Consider the following features:
1. Consent of the governed
2. Political equality
3. Accountability of the ruled to the ruler

Which of the above feature/features outline democratic rule?
75149.sol:
Democracy is a form of government in which the rulers are elected by the people. The fundamental principles of democratic rule include the consent of the governed, meaning the government's legitimacy and moral right to use state power is justified and lawful only when consented to by the people or society over which that political power is exercised.

Political equality is another core feature, ensuring that all citizens have an equal voice in the political process, typically expressed as 'one person, one vote'.

In a democracy, the rulers (government) are accountable to the ruled (citizens), not the other way around. The statement 'Accountability of the ruled to the ruler' contradicts democratic principles and is a feature of authoritarian regimes.

Therefore, only features 1 and 2 outline democratic rule.

Answer: 1 and 2 only

77031.subject: Mathematics
77031.text: Consider the following statements:I. $y = xe^{2x}$ is the solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$ y $\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)$.II. $y = x\ln|x| + cx$ is the solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + y}{x}.$Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
77031.sol:
For Statement I:

Given $y = xe^{2x}$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{2x} + 2xe^{2x} = e^{2x}(1 + 2x)$

Also, $y\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right) = xe^{2x} \left(\dfrac{2x + 1}{x}\right) =$e^{2x}(2x + 1)$

Since \dfrac{dy}{dx} =$ y$\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right), Statement I is correct.

For Statement II:

Given $ y = x\ln|x| + cx$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \ln|$ x| + x$\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) +$ c = \ln|x| + 1 + c$

Also, \dfrac{x + y}{x} =1 + \dfrac{y}{x} =1 + \dfrac{x\ln|x| + cx}{x} =1 + \ln|x| + c$

Since $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + y}{x},Statement II is correct.

Both statements I$ and II are correct.

Answer: Both I and II

options: The shoot and root die together
Neither root nor shoot will die
80646.sol: In a ring girdled plant the root dies first. Like all vascular plants, trees use two vascular tissues for transportation of water and nutrients: the xylem (also known as the wood), and the phloem (the innermost layer of the bark). Girdling results in the removal of the phloem, and death occurs from the inability of the leaves to transport sugars (primarily sucrose) to the roots. This is an experiment to prove the translocation of food through the phloem.

83259.subject: Physics
83259.text:
Savitha, a XI standard student, while conducting an experiment to determine the effective length of a simple pendulum L, notes down the data of time taken to complete $30$ oscillations as $60$ s and hence calculates the length of the simple pendulum as :
(Take $\pi^2 = 9.8$, and $g = 9.8$ m/s$^2$)
83259.sol:
Time period $T = \dfrac{60}{30} = 2$ s.

The formula for the time period of a simple pendulum is $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}$.

Squaring both sides, we get $T^2 = 4\pi^2 \dfrac{L}{g}$.

Substituting the given values $T = 2$ s, $\pi^2 = 9.8$, and $g = 9.8$ m/s$^2$:

$(2)^2 = 4 \times 9.8 \times \dfrac{L}{9.8}$

$4 = 4L$

$L = 1$ m.

Answer: $1$ m

84278.subject: Zoology
84278.text: Which one of the following is not a second messenger in hormone action?
84278.sol:
Second messengers are the organic molecules whose production or release usually amplifies a signal such as a hormone and are received at the cell surface.
Sodium (Na) is not a second messenger in hormone action.
Related Theory
Second messengers are molecules that relay signals received at receptors on the cell surface such as the arrival of protein hormones, growth factors, etc. to target molecules in the cytosol and/or nucleus. Second messengers also serve to greatly amplify the strength of the signal. Binding of a ligand to a single receptor at the cell surface may end up causing massive changes in the biochemical activities within the cell. There are 3 major classes of second messengers:
(i) cyclic nucleotides (e.g., cAMPand cGMP)
(ii) inositol trisphosphate (IP3) and diacylglycerol (DAG)
(iii) calcium ions $\left(\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}\right)$

102422.subject: Physics
102422.text: A block of mass $m$ attached to a spring oscillates with a time period $T$ on the surface of the Earth. The entire spring-mass system is then taken to a planet where the acceleration due to gravity is one-fourth that of the Earth, and the block is replaced by another block of mass $2m$. The new time period of oscillation will be:
102422.sol:
The time period of a spring-mass system is given by $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$, where $m$ is the mass of the block and $k$ is the spring constant.

The time period is independent of the acceleration due to gravity ($g$). Therefore, taking the system to a planet with $g' = \dfrac{g}{4}$ has no effect on the time period.

When the mass is changed to $m' = 2m$, the new time period is:
$T' = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{2m}{k}} = \sqrt{2} \left( 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}} \right) = \sqrt{2}T$.

Answer: $\sqrt{2}T$

102652.subject: Physics
102652.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: For an open organ pipe, the $n^{th}$ overtone always contains $(n+1)$ displacement nodes.

Statement II: For a pipe closed at one end, the $n^{th}$ harmonic (where $n$ is an odd integer) always contains $n$ displacement nodes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
102652.sol:
Evaluate Statement I:
For an open organ pipe, the $n^{th}$ overtone corresponds to the $(n+1)^{th}$ harmonic. The number of displacement nodes in the $p^{th}$ harmonic of an open pipe is $p$. Therefore, the $(n+1)^{th}$ harmonic contains $(n+1)$ displacement nodes. Statement I is correct.

Evaluate Statement II:
For a pipe closed at one end, only odd harmonics are present. The $n^{th}$ harmonic (where $n$ is an odd integer) contains $\dfrac{n+1}{2}$ displacement nodes, not $n$ nodes. For example, the $3^{rd}$ harmonic contains $\dfrac{3+1}{2} = 2$ displacement nodes. Statement II is incorrect.

Therefore, Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

103150.subject: Physics
103150.text:
A parallel plate capacitor with circular plates of radius $10 \text{ cm}$ has a capacitance of $50 \text{ \mu F}$. It is being charged by a source such that the potential difference across its plates is changing at a rate of $20 \text{ V s}^{-1}$. The magnitude of the induced magnetic field exactly at the outer edge of the capacitor plates is:
(Given $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \text{ T m A}^{-1}$)
103150.sol:
The displacement current between the capacitor plates is given by:
$I_d = C \dfrac{dV}{dt}$
$I_d = 50 \times 10^{-6} \times 20 = 10^{-3} \text{ A}$

According to the Ampere-Maxwell law, the line integral of the magnetic field around the edge of the plates is equal to $\mu_0$ times the total displacement current enclosed:
$\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 I_d$
$B(2\pi R) = \mu_0 I_d$

Substituting the given values ($R = 10 \text{ cm} = 0.1 \text{ m}$):
$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_d}{2\pi R}$
$B = \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 10^{-3}}{2\pi \times 0.1}$
$B = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-10}}{0.1} = 2 \times 10^{-9} \text{ T}$

Option 1 is incorrect as a changing electric field induces a magnetic field even in the absence of conduction current.
Option 3 is incorrect as it misses the $2\pi$ factor in the denominator.
Option 4 is incorrect as it divides by the area $\pi R^2$ instead of the circumference $2\pi R$.

Answer: $2 \times 10^{-9} \text{ T}$

103280.subject: Physics
103280.text: A cell of emf $6 \mathrm{~V}$ and internal resistance $1 \Omega$ is connected across a parallel combination of two identical external resistors of $4 \Omega$ each. The terminal potential difference of the cell is:
103280.sol:
The equivalent resistance of the two $4 \Omega$ resistors in parallel is:
$R_{\text{eq}} = \dfrac{4 \times 4}{4 + 4} = 2 \Omega$

The total resistance of the circuit, including the internal resistance $r$, is:
$R_{\text{total}} = R_{\text{eq}} + r = 2 + 1 = 3 \Omega$

The current drawn from the cell is:
$i = \dfrac{E}{R_{\text{total}}} = \dfrac{6}{3} = 2 \mathrm{~A}$

The terminal potential difference $V$ across the cell is the voltage across the equivalent external resistance:
$V = i \times R_{\text{eq}} = 2 \times 2 = 4 \mathrm{~V}$

Alternatively, using the cell formula:
$V = E - ir = 6 - (2 \times 1) = 4 \mathrm{~V}$

Answer: $4 \mathrm{~V}$

104033.subject: Physics
104033.text:
A series LCR circuit is connected to a $45sin ( \omegat )$ Volt source. The resonant angular frequency of the circuit is ${10}^{5}rad{s}^{- 1}$ and current amplitude at resonance is ${I}_{0}$. When the angular frequency of the source is $\omega = 8 \times {10}^{4}rad{s}^{- 1}$, the current amplitude in the circuit is $0 . 05{I}_{0}$. If $L = 50mH$, match each entry in List-$I$ with an appropriate value from List-$II$ and choose the correct option.

  List-$I$   List-$II$
$P$ ${I}_{0}$ in $mA$ $1$ $44 . 4$
$Q$ The quality factor of the circuit $2$ $18$
$R$ The bandwidth of the circuit in $rad{s}^{- 1}$ $3$ $400$
$S$ The peak power dissipated at resonance in Watt $4$ $2250$
    $5$ $500$
104033.sol:
Resonant angular frequency is given by, $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = {10}^{5}$

$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\left(50 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)C}} = {10}^{5} ⇒ C = 2 \times {10}^{- 9}F$

Given: $V = 45sin\left(\omegat\right)$. Therefore, ${V}_{0} = 45$.

Now, ${I}_{0} = \dfrac{{V}_{0}}{R} = \dfrac{45}{R} . . . \left(ii\right)$

Inductive reactance, ${X}_{L} = \omegaL = \left(8 \times {10}^{4}\right) \times \left(50 \times {10}^{- 3}\right) = 4000Ω$.

and capacitive reactance, ${X}_{C} = \dfrac{1}{\omegaC} = \dfrac{1}{\left(8 \times {10}^{4}\right) \times \left(2 \times {10}^{- 9}\right)} = 6250Ω$.

For new current amplitude, we can write

$0 . 05{I}_{0} = \dfrac{45}{\sqrt{{R}^{2} + {\left({X}_{L} - {X}_{C}\right)}^{2}}} ⇒ 0 . 05{I}_{0} = \dfrac{45}{\sqrt{{R}^{2} + {\left(6250 - 4000\right)}^{2}}} ⇒ 0 . 05 \times \dfrac{45}{R} = \dfrac{45}{\sqrt{{R}^{2} + {\left(6250 - 4000\right)}^{2}}} ⇒ {R}^{2} + {\left(6250 - 4000\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{{R}^{2}}{{\left(0 . 05\right)}^{2}} ⇒ {R}^{2} + {\left(2250\right)}^{2} = 400{R}^{2} ⇒ R = \dfrac{2250}{\sqrt{399}} = 112 . 67Ω$

Where ${X}_{{L}_{0}} = {X}_{{C}_{0}}$ are at resonant frequencies

On solving, $⇒ {I}_{0} = \dfrac{45}{R} ≃ 400mA$

Quality factor $Q = \dfrac{{X}_{L}}{R} ≃ 44 . 44$

Now, $Q = \dfrac{{\omega}_{0}}{∆ \omega} ⇒ ∆ \omega ≃ 2250rad{s}^{- 1}$.

Peak power $= 45 \times \dfrac{400}{1000}W = 18W$

Therefore, $P \to 3, Q \to 1, R \to 4, S \to 2$.

104489.subject: Physics
104489.text: An object is placed at a distance of $30$ cm in front of a convex lens of focal length $20$ cm. A convex mirror is placed coaxially $20$ cm behind the lens. If the final image formed by the combination coincides with the object itself, the focal length of the convex mirror is :
104489.sol:
For the convex lens:
Object distance, $u = -30$ cm
Focal length, $f = +20$ cm
Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{60}$
$\Rightarrow v = +60$ cm
The convex lens forms an image $60$ cm to its right.

The convex mirror is placed $20$ cm behind the lens. The image formed by the lens acts as a virtual object for the mirror, located at a distance of $60 - 20 = 40$ cm behind the mirror.

For the final image to coincide with the object, the rays refracted by the lens must strike the convex mirror normally. This means the rays must be directed towards the center of curvature of the mirror.
Therefore, the center of curvature is at the position of the virtual object, which is $40$ cm behind the mirror.
Radius of curvature, $R = 40$ cm.
The focal length of the convex mirror is $f_m = \dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{40}{2} = 20$ cm.

Answer: $20$ cm

105274.text:
Read the following statements describing the potential configurations of a p-n junction diode:
(A) The p-side is earthed and the n-side is at $-2\text{ V}$.
(B) The p-side is at $-3\text{ V}$ and the n-side is at $-1\text{ V}$.
(C) The p-side is at $+2\text{ V}$ and the n-side is at $+5\text{ V}$.
(D) The p-side is at $-1\text{ V}$ and the n-side is at $-4\text{ V}$.

How many of the given statements describe a reverse-biased diode?
105274.sol:
A diode is reverse-biased when the potential at the p-side ($V_p$) is less than the potential at the n-side ($V_n$).

Statement (A): $V_p = 0\text{ V}$ (earthed), $V_n = -2\text{ V}$. Since $0 > -2$, it is forward-biased.

Statement (B): $V_p = -3\text{ V}$, $V_n = -1\text{ V}$. Since $-3 < -1$, it is reverse-biased.

Statement (C): $V_p = 2\text{ V}$, $V_n = 5\text{ V}$. Since $2 < 5$, it is reverse-biased.

Statement (D): $V_p = -1\text{ V}$, $V_n = -4\text{ V}$. Since $-1 > -4$, it is forward-biased.

Statements (B) and (C) describe a reverse-biased diode. Therefore, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Two

111914.subject: Chemistry
111914.text:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) The permanent effect that is weaker than the electromeric effect when they operate in opposite directions(I) Electromeric effect
(B) Temporary complete transfer of $\pi$ electrons in the presence of an attacking reagent(II) Hyperconjugation
(C) Delocalisation of $\sigma$ electrons of a C-H bond into an adjacent $\pi$ system(III) Resonance effect
(D) Polarity produced in a molecule by the interaction of two $\pi$ bonds or a $\pi$ bond and lone pair(IV) Inductive effect

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
111914.sol:
(A) When the inductive and electromeric effects operate in opposite directions, the temporary electromeric effect predominates over the permanent inductive effect. Thus, (A) matches with Inductive effect (IV).

(B) The electromeric effect involves the temporary complete transfer of shared $\pi$ electrons to one of the atoms joined by a multiple bond on the demand of an attacking reagent. Thus, (B) matches with Electromeric effect (I).

(C) Hyperconjugation involves the delocalisation of $\sigma$ electrons of a C-H bond of an alkyl group directly attached to an atom of an unsaturated system or to an atom with an unshared $p$ orbital. Thus, (C) matches with Hyperconjugation (II).

(D) The resonance effect is defined as the polarity produced in the molecule by the interaction of two $\pi$-bonds or between a $\pi$-bond and lone pair of electrons present on an adjacent atom. Thus, (D) matches with Resonance effect (III).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)

114362.subject: Chemistry
114362.text: Consider the theoretical plots of molar conductivity ($\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}$) versus $\sqrt{c}$ for aqueous solutions of $\mathrm{NaCl}$, $\mathrm{KCl}$, and $\mathrm{CaCl}_2$ at $298\text{ K}$. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: The plots for $\mathrm{NaCl}$ and $\mathrm{CaCl}_2$ are parallel to each other because both contain chloride ions.
The plots for $\mathrm{NaCl}$ and $\mathrm{KCl}$ have the same intercept on the y-axis because they are the same type of electrolyte.
The plots for $\mathrm{NaCl}$ and $\mathrm{KCl}$ are parallel to each other, but they have different intercepts on the y-axis.
The plots for all three electrolytes have the same slope because they are all strong electrolytes.
114362.sol:
According to the Debye-Hückel-Onsager equation, $\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}} = \Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ} - \mathrm{A} \sqrt{c}$.

The slope of the plot is $-\mathrm{A}$. The value of the constant 'A' depends on the type of electrolyte (charges on the cation and anion).

$\mathrm{NaCl}$ and $\mathrm{KCl}$ are both 1-1 electrolytes, so they have the same value of 'A'. Thus, their plots will have the same slope and be parallel to each other.

The intercept on the y-axis is the limiting molar conductivity ($\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ}$). According to Kohlrausch's law, $\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ}$ depends on the specific limiting ionic conductivities of the constituent ions. Since $\mathrm{Na}^+$ and $\mathrm{K}^+$ have different limiting ionic conductivities, $\mathrm{NaCl}$ and $\mathrm{KCl}$ will have different intercepts.

$\mathrm{CaCl}_2$ is a 2-1 electrolyte, so it has a different value of 'A' and its plot will not be parallel to that of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ or $\mathrm{KCl}$.

Answer: The plots for $\mathrm{NaCl}$ and $\mathrm{KCl}$ are parallel to each other, but they have different intercepts on the y-axis.

114906.subject: Chemistry
114906.text: For a reaction $A + B \rightarrow \text{Products}$, the rate constant has the unit $\text{L}^{2}\ \text{mol}^{-2}\ \text{s}^{-1}$. If the reaction is first order with respect to reactant $A$, what is the order of the reaction with respect to reactant $B$?
114906.sol:
The general unit for the rate constant $k$ of an $n$-th order reaction is $(\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1})^{1-n}\ \text{s}^{-1}$.

The given unit is $\text{L}^{2}\ \text{mol}^{-2}\ \text{s}^{-1}$, which can be rewritten as $(\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1})^{-2}\ \text{s}^{-1}$.

Equating the exponents:
$1 - n = -2$
$n = 3$

The overall order of the reaction is $3$.

The overall order is the sum of the partial orders with respect to each reactant:
Overall order = Order with respect to $A$ + Order with respect to $B$
$3 = 1 + \text{Order with respect to } B$
$\text{Order with respect to } B = 2$

Answer: 2

117759.subject: Chemistry
117759.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For the same metal, same oxidation state and same ligands, the crystal field splitting energy in a tetrahedral complex ($\Delta_t$) is approximately $\dfrac{4}{9}$ of that in an octahedral complex ($\Delta_o$).

Reason (R): Tetrahedral complexes rarely form low-spin configurations.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
117759.sol:
Assertion (A) is a correct statement. According to Crystal Field Theory, for the same metal ion, same oxidation state and same ligands, the relationship between tetrahedral and octahedral crystal field splitting energies is given by $\Delta_t = \dfrac{4}{9} \Delta_o$.

Reason (R) is also a correct statement. In tetrahedral complexes, the crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_t$) is generally smaller than the pairing energy ($P$). As a result, electrons prefer to occupy higher energy orbitals rather than pairing up, so low-spin configurations are rarely observed.

However, Reason (R) is a consequence of the small magnitude of $\Delta_t$, not the explanation for why $\Delta_t = \dfrac{4}{9} \Delta_o$. The factor of $\dfrac{4}{9}$ arises because there are only 4 ligands instead of 6, and they do not point directly at the $d$-orbitals.

Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

121691.subject: Botany
121691.text: Which of the following characteristics is true of algae?
121691.sol: <mark>Algae are chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic (both freshwater and marine) organisms</mark>. They occur in a variety of other habitats: moist stones, soils and wood. Some of them also occur in association with fungi (lichen) and animals (e.g., on sloth bear). The form and size of algae is highly variable, ranging from colonial forms like Volvox and the filamentous forms like Ulothrix and Spirogyra (Figure 3.1). A few of the marine forms such as kelps, form massive plant bodies.The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina, is termed as anisogamous. Fusion between one large, non- motile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus.

Being photosynthetic they increase the level of dissolved oxygen in their immediate environment. They are of paramount importance as primary producers of energy-rich compounds which form the basis of the food cycles of all aquatic animals. Many species of Porphyra, Laminaria and Sargassum are among the 70 species of marine algae used as food. <mark>Certain marine brown and red algae produce large amounts of hydrocolloids (water holding substances), e.g., algin (brown algae) and carrageen (red algae) which are used commercially.</mark> Agar, one of the commercial products obtained from Gelidium and Gracilaria are used to grow microbes and in preparations of ice-creams and jellies. Chlorella a unicellular alga rich in proteins is used as food supplement even by space travellers. The algae are divided into three main classes: Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae and Rhodophyceae.

122562.text: Which of the following sets of animals exhibit homoiothermy, internal fertilisation, and possess mammary glands?
122562.sol:
The characteristics mentioned (homoiothermy, internal fertilisation, and presence of mammary glands) are defining features of the class Mammalia.

Let us evaluate the given options:
Macropus (Kangaroo) and Camelus (Camel) are mammals, but Psittacula (Parrot) belongs to class Aves. Birds are homoiothermic and have internal fertilisation but lack mammary glands.
Ornithorhynchus (Platypus) is a mammal, but Crocodilus (Crocodile) is a reptile (poikilothermic, lacking mammary glands) and Neophron (Vulture) is a bird.
Pteropus (Flying fox), Delphinus (Common dolphin), and Equus (Horse) all belong to class Mammalia. Therefore, they all exhibit homoiothermy, internal fertilisation, and possess mammary glands.
Balaenoptera (Blue whale) is a mammal, but Pavo (Peacock) is a bird and Rana (Frog) is an amphibian (poikilothermic, external fertilisation, lacking mammary glands).

Answer: Pteropus, Delphinus, Equus

123827.subject: Botany
123827.text:
Read the following cellular events carefully:
X: Centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm of animal cells.
Y: Proteins are synthesized in preparation for mitosis.
Z: Cells remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so.

Identify the cell cycle phases corresponding to the events X, Y, and Z respectively.
options: X - $G_2$ phase, Y - S phase, Z - $G_1$ phase
X - S phase, Y - $G_1$ phase, Z - $G_0$ phase
X - S phase, Y - $G_2$ phase, Z - $G_0$ phase
X - $G_1$ phase, Y - $G_2$ phase, Z - $G_0$ phase
123827.sol:
Event X corresponds to the S phase (synthesis phase). During this phase, DNA replication occurs in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm of animal cells.

Event Y corresponds to the $G_2$ phase. During the $G_2$ phase, proteins are synthesized in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues.

Event Z corresponds to the $G_0$ phase (quiescent stage). Cells in this stage exit the $G_1$ phase and enter an inactive stage where they do not proliferate but remain metabolically active.

Answer: X - S phase, Y - $G_2$ phase, Z - $G_0$ phase

123889.text: A diploid animal cell in the G1 phase of the cell cycle has 16 chromosomes and an initial amount of DNA denoted as 2C. Which of the following correctly represents the number of chromosomes, the amount of DNA, and the number of centrosomes in this cell during the G2 phase?
123889.sol:
During the S phase of the cell cycle, DNA replication occurs, causing the amount of DNA to double. Therefore, the initial DNA amount of 2C in the G1 phase increases to 4C by the G2 phase.

However, there is no increase in the chromosome number during the S phase. A cell that has 16 chromosomes in G1 will still have exactly 16 chromosomes in G2 (though each chromosome now consists of two sister chromatids).

Additionally, in animal cells, the centrosome (containing the centrioles) duplicates in the cytoplasm during the S phase. Thus, the single centrosome present in G1 duplicates to form 2 centrosomes by the G2 phase.

Therefore, in the G2 phase, the cell will have 16 chromosomes, 4C amount of DNA, and 2 centrosomes.

Answer: 16 chromosomes; 4C DNA; 2 centrosomes

124006.subject: Botany
124006.text: What is the process called when molecules move across the membrane without requiring energy?
124006.sol: One of the most important functions of the plasma membrane is the transport of the molecules across it. The membrane is selectively permeable to some molecules present on either side of it. Many molecules can move briefly across the membrane without any requirement of energy and this is called the passive transport. Neutral solutes may move across the membrane by the process of simple diffusion along the concentration gradient, i.e., from higher concentration to the lower. Water may also move across this membrane from higher to lower concentration. Movement of water by diffusion is called osmosis. As the polar molecules cannot pass through the nonpolar lipid bilayer, they require a carrier protein of the membrane to facilitate their transport across the membrane. A few ions or molecules are transported across the membrane against their concentration gradient, i.e., from lower to the higher concentration. Such a transport is an energy dependent process, in which ATP is utilised and is called active transport, e.g., Na+/K+ Pump.
124006.meta: What is the process called when molecules move across the membrane without requiring energy?

124918.subject: Botany
124918.text: Where does the breakdown of complex molecules to yield energy take place in eukaryotes?
124918.sol: Photosynthesis, of course, takes place within the chloroplasts (in the eukaryotes), whereas the breakdown of complex molecules to yield energy takes place in the cytoplasm and in the mitochondria (also only in eukaryotes). The breaking of the C-C bonds of complex compounds through oxidation within the cells, leading to release of considerable amount of energy is called respiration.

125161.subject: Botany
125161.text: A particular respiratory substrate yields a Respiratory Quotient (RQ) of approximately $0.7$. Which of the following statements correctly describes how this substrate, or its components, enter the respiratory pathway?
options: It is degraded by proteases into amino acids, which then enter the pathway as pyruvate or acetyl CoA.
The intact molecule directly enters the Krebs cycle without undergoing any prior enzymatic breakdown.
Upon breakdown, its fatty acid components enter the pathway as PGAL, while glycerol enters as acetyl CoA.
It breaks down into fatty acids and glycerol, where fatty acids enter as acetyl CoA and glycerol enters as PGAL.
125161.sol:
An RQ value of approximately $0.7$ indicates that the respiratory substrate is a fat (e.g., tripalmitin).

According to the amphibolic pathway described in NCERT, fats do not enter the respiratory pathway directly. They must first be broken down into fatty acids and glycerol.

If fatty acids are to be respired, they are degraded to acetyl CoA and then enter the pathway. Glycerol enters the pathway after being converted to PGAL (Phosphoglyceraldehyde).

Option 1 incorrectly describes the breakdown of proteins (which have an RQ of approximately $0.9$).
Option 2 is incorrect because complex molecules must be broken down before entering the pathway.
Option 3 incorrectly swaps the entry points of fatty acids and glycerol.

Answer: It breaks down into fatty acids and glycerol, where fatty acids enter as acetyl CoA and glycerol enters as PGAL.

125337.subject: Botany
125337.text: What is formed in the stroma as a result of enzymatic reactions?
125337.sol: Within the chloroplast there is membranous system consisting of grana, the stroma lamellae, and the matrix stroma. There is a clear division of labour within the chloroplast. The membrane system is responsible for trapping the light energy and also for the synthesis of ATP and NADPH. In stroma, enzymatic reactions synthesise sugar, which in turn forms starch. The former set of reactions, since they are directly light driven are called light reactions (photochemical reactions). The latter are not directly light driven but are dependent on the products of light reactions (ATP and NADPH). Hence, to distinguish the latter they are called, by convention, as dark reactions (carbon reactions). However, this should not be construed to mean that they occur in darkness or that they are not light-dependent.

127152.subject: Botany
127152.text: How many animal species might there be yet to be discovered and described in India?
127152.sol: Although India has only 2.4 per cent of the world’s land area, its share of the global species diversity is an impressive 8.1 per cent. That is what makes our country one of the 12 mega diversity countries of the world. Nearly 45,000 species of plants and twice as many of animals have been recorded from India. How many living species are actually there waiting to be discovered and named? If we accept May’s global estimates, only 22 per cent of the total species have been recorded so far. Applying this proportion to India’s diversity figures, we estimate that there are probably more than 1,00,000 plant species and more than 3,00,000 animal species yet to be discovered and described

127171.subject: Botany
127171.text: What is the range of Z values according to the species:area relationship analysis?
127171.sol: : During his pioneering and extensive explorations in the wilderness of South American jungles, the great German naturalist and geographer Alexander von Humboldt observed that within a region species richness increased with increasing explored area, but only up to a limit. In fact, the relation between species richness and area for a wide variety of taxa (angiosperm plants, birds, bats, freshwater fishes) turns out to be a rectangular hyperbola (Figure13.2). On a logarithmic scale, the relationship is a straight line described by the equation log S = log C + Z log A where S= Species richness A= Area Z = slope of the line (regression coefficient) C = Y-intercept Ecologists have discovered that the value of Z lies in the range of 0.1 to 0.2, regardless of the taxonomic group or the region (whether it is the plants in Britain, birds in California or molluscs in New York state, the slopes of the regression line are amazingly similar). But, if you analyse the species-area relationships among very large areas like the entire continents, you will find that the slope of the line to be much steeper (Z values in the range of 0.6 to 1.2).
127171.meta: What is the range of Z values according to the species:area relationship analysis?
